signing.rsa_public_exponent: odd integer greater than or equal to 3
signing.key_rotation: new signing keys must be published in JWKS before tokens using them are issued

lifetime.refresh_model: issue a new short-lived service credential; do not extend an existing token

security_requirements: private signing keys never leave GoreeCloud Identity
runtime private-key files must be regular, non-symlinked, size-bounded, and owner-only on POSIX before PEM parsing
source-level runtime key-file hardening does not substitute for durable production signing-key custody or managed key lifecycle acceptance
producer systems must not self-sign, mint, or substitute GoreeCloud Mesh service credentials
tokens must use the RS256/JWT protected-header profile and must not direct consumers to alternate or embedded verification keys
tokens must not contain user content, secrets, backup payloads, prompts, or private application data
service_id must match the authenticated workload identity represented by sub
consumers must validate signature, protected-header profile, issuer, audience, expiry, not-before, service identity, required scope, kid profile, RSA key strength, and RSA public exponent
JWKS consumers must require application/json and must reject redirected or otherwise untrusted key-source transport
unknown or invalid kid, unsupported algorithm, missing required claim, malformed scope, invalid key material, or invalid temporal claim must fail closed
transitional framework integrations must delegate service-token semantics to the native goreecloud_identity authority
deployment_boundary: The first-party GoreeCloud Identity token authority and JWKS generation are implemented in the native goreecloud_identity package. The runtime file loader now rejects symlinks, non-regular files, oversized key material, and POSIX key files readable or writable by group/other users before PEM parsing. The protected-header contract is aligned with the Mesh verifier and does not permit token-selected key sources. This is source-level key-custody and token-profile hardening only: production acceptance still requires durable Identity-managed signing-key storage, a deployed native or explicitly approved transitional JWKS endpoint, live service-token issuance, rotation evidence, successful end-to-end Mesh verification, and completion of the broader native Identity rebuild.
